userStories.title: Phase M: exclude completed stories from semantic dedup comparison set
userStories.description: Phase M currently compares every new story candidate against ALL stories in prd.json, including the 309+ completed ones (passes: true). This means a new story about 'improving X' gets rejected as a near-duplicate of the completed story 'implement X', even though they are genuinely different work. The dedup filter should only compare new candidates against PENDING stories (passes: false). Completed stories are done — a candidate that resembles a completed story is an extension or improvement, not a true duplicate. Fix lib/merge_stories.py (or the relevant dedup function): when building the comparison corpus, filter to only stories where passes is False.

userStories.title: Parallel workers: replace raw results.tsv appends with locked_append helper
userStories.description: Multiple Ralph workers append to results.tsv simultaneously using raw printf >> redirections with no file locking. On Windows NTFS, concurrent unbuffered appends from separate processes can interleave bytes mid-line, producing garbled TSV rows or missing newlines. Implement a thin shell wrapper lib/core/locked_append_tsv.sh (or a Python helper similar to locked_append_jsonl in spiral_io.py) that acquires an exclusive flock/lockfile before appending and releases it after. Replace every raw >> results.tsv append in run_parallel_ralph.sh and ralph.sh with this wrapper. The lock file should be worker-local (per WTREE) to avoid cross-worktree contention; the main-thread merge step can use the repo-root lock.

userStories.title: Parallel workers: atomic compare-and-swap for prd.json updates in worker worktrees
userStories.description: Workers update their local WTREE/prd.json using jq read-modify-write cycles: read file -> modify in memory -> write tmp -> mv tmp to prd.json. When two sub-processes within the same worker (e.g. the main ralph loop and the retry handler) hit the same file concurrently, the second write overwrites the first silently. Introduce an atomic_patch_prd() shell function in lib/core/prd_lock.sh that: (1) acquires a per-WTREE lockfile (mkdir-based, PID recorded), (2) reads prd.json, (3) applies the jq transform passed as argument, (4) writes atomically (tmp+mv), (5) releases the lock. Replace all bare jq...prd.json.tmp && mv patterns in run_parallel_ralph.sh, retry.sh, decompose.sh, and commit_revert.sh with atomic_patch_prd() calls.
acceptanceCriteria: lib/core/prd_lock.sh exports atomic_patch_prd <wtree> <jq-filter> function

userStories.title: Parallel workers: use millisecond-precision timestamps to prevent branch name collisions
userStories.description: Branch names for worker worktrees are derived from TIMESTAMP=$(date +%s) which has 1-second granularity. Two Spiral runs starting within the same second produce identical branch names (e.g. spiral-worker-1-1712345600), causing git to reject the second creation and fall back to detached HEAD — silently losing patch tracking. Fix: replace date +%s with date +%s%3N (epoch milliseconds) everywhere TIMESTAMP is used for branch naming. Also append a short random suffix ($RANDOM) to guarantee uniqueness even on systems where date lacks %N support (Windows Git Bash). Update the branch-name regex in run_parallel_ralph.sh cleanup code to match the new format.
acceptanceCriteria: TIMESTAMP variable uses millisecond precision (date +%s%3N) with $RANDOM fallback for Windows Git Bash compatibility

userStories.title: Parallel workers: transactional patch application with rollback on partial failure
userStories.description: Patches from completed workers are applied sequentially in run_parallel_ralph.sh (Step 7). If patch N fails (disk full, conflict, git error), patches 1..N-1 are already committed with no rollback, leaving the codebase in a broken intermediate state. Add a savepoint before patch application: (1) record current HEAD SHA, (2) apply all patches in sequence, (3) if ANY patch fails, revert to the saved SHA (git reset --hard to savepoint) and emit a structured error listing which patches succeeded and which failed. Workers whose patches were rolled back have their story status reset to pending in prd.json. Log the rollback event to spiral_events.jsonl as patch_rollback with the list of affected story IDs.

userStories.title: Parallel workers: run ruff + mypy on merged diff before committing to catch semantic conflicts
userStories.description: git merge-tree detects textual conflicts but misses semantic ones: Worker A changes a function signature in api.py while Worker B adds a call-site using the old signature in a non-overlapping line. The patch applies cleanly, but the code is broken at runtime. After all worker patches are applied (Step 7) and before the final commit, run a fast static analysis pass: (1) ruff check on changed Python files (git diff --name-only HEAD~1..HEAD filtered to *.py), (2) mypy --no-error-summary on the same files. If either tool reports errors, emit a semantic_conflict event to spiral_events.jsonl, rollback the merge, mark conflicting workers stories as pending, and log the linter output. Add SPIRAL_SEMANTIC_CHECK=true/false toggle in spiral.config.sh (default true).

userStories.title: Parallel workers: replace hardcoded docker lock timeout with adaptive PID-aware backoff
userStories.description: The docker mutex in run_parallel_ralph.sh uses a hardcoded 120-iteration wait loop (1s sleep each = 120s max). On slow systems or during heavy I/O, legitimate docker pull/build operations exceed 120s, causing a healthy worker to assume lock-holder crash and break the mutex — allowing two workers to run docker commands simultaneously and corrupt container state. Replace the fixed loop with: (1) exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s... capped at 30s), (2) detect if lock-holder PID (stored in the lock directory as a pid file) is still alive (kill -0 $pid), (3) only break the lock if the PID is dead AND the lock is older than SPIRAL_DOCKER_LOCK_TIMEOUT (default 300s). Store the PID in a file inside the lock directory on acquisition.
acceptanceCriteria: Docker lock acquisition writes holder PID to $LOCK_DIR/pid file
Wait loop uses exponential backoff (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 30s) instead of fixed 1s sleep
Lock is only broken if holder PID is dead AND lock age > SPIRAL_DOCKER_LOCK_TIMEOUT (default 300)
SPIRAL_DOCKER_LOCK_TIMEOUT configurable in spiral.config.sh
If a live PID holds the lock past SPIRAL_DOCKER_LOCK_TIMEOUT, emit a warning but keep waiting
Test: simulate a stale lock with dead PID and verify cleanup after timeout

userStories.title: Parallel workers: add timeout and respawn for idle worker pool processes
userStories.description: Worker pool processes (pre-warming) wait indefinitely for task files to appear in .worker-pool/worker-N/task. If the main coordinator fails to write the task file (disk full, crash, permission error), the pool worker hangs forever consuming memory with no visibility. Add: (1) a configurable SPIRAL_POOL_TASK_TIMEOUT (default 120s) after which an idle pool worker logs a warning and exits cleanly, (2) when a pool worker exits due to timeout, write a pool_worker_timeout event to spiral_events.jsonl with worker_id and waited_seconds, (3) the main coordinator detects timed-out pool workers and respawns them up to SPIRAL_POOL_RESPAWN_LIMIT (default 3) times before giving up and falling back to non-pooled execution.
acceptanceCriteria: Pool workers exit after SPIRAL_POOL_TASK_TIMEOUT seconds of idle waiting (default 120)
On timeout exit, pool_worker_timeout event written to spiral_events.jsonl
Main coordinator detects pool worker exit and respawns up to SPIRAL_POOL_RESPAWN_LIMIT times
After exhausting respawn limit, fallback to non-pooled worker launch with a warning log
SPIRAL_POOL_TASK_TIMEOUT and SPIRAL_POOL_RESPAWN_LIMIT configurable in spiral.config.sh
No change in behavior when task files are delivered on time
